newsitem.title: CHINA: Akzo Nobel sees China sales tripling.
newsitem.headline: Akzo Nobel sees China sales tripling.

text.p: Dutch chemicals group Akzo Nobel NV forecast on Wednesday that its turnover in China would triple to $800 million in five years.
Akzo Nobel envisaged pouring more than $300 million into China over the next five years, group vice-chairman Herman van Karnebeek told reporters in Beijing.
It was looking into setting up a $200 million joint venture with China's Wuxi Taiji Ltd in industrial polyester fibres in the city of Wuxi near Shanghai, he said.
Separately, Akzo Nobel was mulling a $100 million joint venture with Shanghai Petrochemical, van Karnebeek said. He declined to elaborate on the planned deals.

Akzo Nobel has thus far invested $80 million in six joint ventures in China. It announced on Wednesday the establishment of a seventh joint venture, which made Akzo Nobel the biggest manufacturer of choline chloride in China.

Akzo Nobel invested $3.0 million for a 65 percent stake in the choline chloride joint venture in Yixing in eastern Jiangsu province, executives said. The Chinese partner is Yixing Choline Chloride Factory. The new venture will have annual production capacity of 200,000 tonnes.
